correctness.rationale: For p>=5, every signed cyclotomic determinant has group-ring coefficient l1 norm <=8 and augmentation zero. Divisibility by Phi_{p^k}, whose p equally spaced monomials give coefficient fibers, forces it to be the zero group-ring element. The odd-order product identity and invertibility of two then give exhaustive C/A/B congruences. A disjoint p-square incidence count yields the closed formula; p=3 is separately proved at order 9 with exact modular nonvanishing certificates. Exhaustive checker tests over more than six million 2x2 minors match all stated hypotheses. The proof explicitly does not extend the short-sum step to p=3,k>2.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial dependencies of odd cyclic Fourier sampling matrices control local two-coordinate interpolation and support/uncertainty behavior. The theorem gives an exact modular description across an infinite prime-power family, a closed p-square census, and the unexpected N=9 all-nonzero two-minor exception despite a zero entry; these are motivated structural consequences rather than a mere fixed-table recomputation.
